_doc: Situation -> theme/state seed map. The curated lens that turns how-people-actually-arrive (a life situation, not a slug) into constellation seeds. Each situation carries: `description` (used by the LLM router to classify free text), `phrasings` (used by the offline keyword fallback), and `seeds` (canonical nodes from merge-map.csv that the constellation engine pools on). Routing: situation_router.py -> claude-haiku-4-5 classifier (free text -> slug) with a graceful keyword fallback when no API key/SDK is present. Seeds are validated against the canonical vocabulary by check_situation_seeds.py.

situations.description: The person feels their outward religious practice doesn't match their inner state — going through the motions, performing faith, fearing they are secretly a fraud.
The person is holding onto resentment toward someone who wronged them and is struggling to let go or forgive.
The person is worried about provision — rent, debt, job loss, not having enough — and the fear of material insecurity.
The person feels spiritually numb or disconnected — worship feels empty, the heart feels hard, they can't feel God the way they used to.
The person is exhausted and on the verge of quitting — life feels like too much to carry and they want to stop.
The person has lost someone to death and is in mourning — heartbroken, missing them, grappling with absence.
The person was betrayed or turned on by family or those closest to them — the wound is from people who should have protected them.
The person is wrestling with whether they still believe — uncertainty about faith itself, questioning if any of it is real.
The person feels far from God and wants to return — they've drifted, lost their way, and long to come back.
The person is eaten up by envy or jealousy — comparing themselves to others who seem to have more, resenting others' blessings.
The person is fighting a recurring temptation or desire they keep giving in to — the pull of the lower self toward something they know is wrong.
The person recognizes pride or arrogance in themselves — feeling superior, self-made, better than others — and is uneasy about it.
The person is gripped by fear of dying — mortality, what comes after, the unknown of the grave and the hereafter.
The person has been wronged or oppressed and no earthly justice is coming — they want vindication and struggle to bear the unfairness.
The person is weighed down by guilt over their past — ashamed of things they did, unsure they can be forgiven.
The person is consumed by ambition, status, or work — chasing more, never satisfied, sensing the pursuit is hollow.
The person notices they take their blessings for granted — never content, always focused on what's missing.
The person feels alone and uncared for — isolated, like no one is there for them, including, at times, God.
The person is worried about their kids — their safety, their faith, the world they're growing up in, their own adequacy as a parent.
The person feels their faith is being challenged on intellectual grounds — science, reason, or argument seem to contradict belief.
The person has encountered a scholarly or polemical critique of the Quran (authorship, contradictions, historicity) and wants a rigorous, honest response, not reassurance.
phrasings: is the quran really from god

situations.description: A parent's child has asked a difficult question about God, a hard verse, suffering, or hell, and the parent needs a grounded, shareable answer.
phrasings: how do i explain to my child

situations.description: The person's marriage or close relationship is under strain — conflict, distance, resentment between spouses or partners.
The person is angry or bitter toward God — feels let down, asks why this was allowed to happen to them, struggles with the justice of their suffering.
The person is caught in an addiction or compulsive habit they keep relapsing into and feel powerless against.
The person feels worse about their life from scrolling — everyone else's highlight reel makes them feel behind, inadequate, or envious.
The person is questioning what they're doing with their life — career feels meaningless, unsure of their purpose or calling.
phrasings: what am i doing with my life

situations.description: The person or a loved one has received a serious diagnosis or is gravely ill — fear, helplessness, and the search for meaning in the suffering.
The person is trapped in a shame spiral — convinced they are irredeemable, that their sin is too great, that God could not forgive them.
The person faces a hard choice and is frozen — afraid of choosing wrong, seeking certainty before they can move.
The person is anxious about what's coming — dread about the future generally, catastrophizing, unable to feel secure about tomorrow.
The person has had a moment of awe — at nature, the cosmos, the order of creation — and wants to deepen that wonder into worship.
The person wants to grow — to purify themselves, build discipline, become a better version of who they are.
The person prays and feels unheard — like their dua goes nowhere, like God isn't paying attention to their particular struggle.
The person is distressed by large-scale injustice — oppression, war, suffering of the innocent — and struggles to reconcile it with a just God.
phrasings: where is god in all this

situations.description: The person was wounded by other religious people or their community — judgment, hypocrisy, exclusion — and it's shaking their relationship with the faith itself.
The person has wronged someone else and wants to repair it — seeking to make amends, return a right, restore a relationship they damaged.
